### Law_ProgressIsEval

// Progress is Eval under a readable name.
Law_ProgressIsEval(f: IEasingFunction, t: Number): Boolean
    => f.Progress(t).LawEq(f.Eval(t));

```plato
//==
// # Easing — derived functions for IEasingFunction
//
// Bodies for the `IEasingFunction` interface declared in `easing.concepts.plato`
// (the concrete easing types live in `easing.types.plato`). An easing
// function inherits `IProcedural<Number, Number>`, so its sole operation is
// `Eval`; the helpers below rename and recombine that single evaluation
// (progress, remaining, mirrored and reversed playback, overshoot and
// anticipation tests). Pure expressions only; all inputs are immutable and
// evaluation is side-effect free. See `README.md` for naming and unit
// conventions.

library Easing
{
    //==
    // # IEasingFunction
    //
    // A pure map from normalized time to normalized progress, inheriting
    // IProcedural<Number, Number> (its sole operation is Eval). Eval(0) is 0 and
    // Eval(1) is 1; intermediate values may leave [0, 1] (overshoot,
    // anticipation). Helpers rename and recombine that single evaluation
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inbetweening).

    // The eased progress at normalized time t; a readable spelling of Eval.
    Progress(self: IEasingFunction, t: Number): Number
        => self.Eval(t);
```

See also: [Library guide](../../../library/README.md).
